## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This one-fascicle text by [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) Śikṣānanda is the third Chinese rendering of the *Avataṃsaka*-family material on the Tathāgata's wisdom and virtue, after [T0302](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0051) (anonymous Qín-period) and [T0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0052) ([闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) Jñānagupta, Suí). The Taishō apparatus's parallel-listing confirms the three-way correspondence.

**Abstract**

The translation belongs to [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) Śikṣānanda's mature Cháng'ān 長安 period, c. 695 – 710 CE; the bracket adopted here reflects this window. As with [T0301](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050) and several other smaller *Avataṃsaka*-tradition translations Śikṣānanda undertook alongside the great *[80-fascicle Huáyán 華嚴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010)*, this version provides the canonical Tang rendering of material that had been translated multiple times before, and would become the authoritative version in subsequent East Asian Buddhist study.

The triple-translation history of this material — anonymous Qín → Jñānagupta Suí → Śikṣānanda Tang — provides one of the clearest cases for the comparative-philological study of the development of Chinese Buddhist translation conventions across the late-fourth to early-eighth centuries.

The Taishō text (T0304) is established on the standard apparatus.
